references.text: Here we find the genealogy of Terah, Abraham's father, who is mentioned in Joshua 24:2 as one who lived on the other side of the river.
Terah took Abram and his family from Ur of the Chaldeans, which was 'on the other side of the river' where they originally lived.
God's call to Abraham to leave his land and his kindred, showing the transition from idol worship to service to the one God.
Reference to the God of Abraham and Nahor, pointing to the family's religious background mentioned in Joshua 24:2.
Abraham was called out of idolatry, confirming that his ancestors served other gods.
Israel's origin from the land of the Canaanites and the region of the Amorites, pointing back to the ancestors' background.
God chose Abram and brought him out from Ur of the Chaldeans, confirming Joshua's words about the original home of the ancestors.
Stephen's speech describes how God revealed himself to Abraham in Mesopotamia before he lived in Haran, and called him out from his land.
